run.help: Run the bots with no window until told to stop (SIGTERM, Ctrl-C; Ctrl-Break on Windows). Refuses with exit 3 if another copy holds the data root; runs the pre-flight first (exit 4, 5 or 6 on a failure). Writes a health line and state/health.json every --health-interval. Not supported for unattended money until EPIC-036B, 036C and 036E have shipped

args.name: --stop-timeout
args.help: Seconds the stop policy may take after the first signal; the whole stop may take this plus 30 (a second signal does not wait). A service unit's TimeoutStopSec must be larger than that sum

args.name: --health-interval
args.help: Seconds between health lines and snapshots

args.name: --on-stop
args.help: What stopping does to the bots: leave-orders (default) closes the workers and leaves resting orders on the exchange; stop-bots stops each active bot first (cancels its orders), for maintenance

args.name: --start-planned
args.help: Start the bots whose applied plan (bot apply) says running and that are at rest. Refused with exit 5, before anything boots, when no plan was applied or the record cannot be read

args.name: --resume-recovering
args.help: Resume every RECOVERING bot, as the Bots tab's Resume does for one: each opens its venue's order session and reconciles with the exchange. Refused (exit 5) unless an alert channel carries bot events or --i-accept-silent-failures is given

args.name: --resume-halted
args.help: Resume every bot that is HALTED or AWAITING_RECOVERY, as a person's Resume and Confirm would: the exchange is read, the order session opened and the proposed ladder laid. A mainnet venue is resumed only with --confirm-venue naming it; the other bots are skipped and left as they are. Refused (exit 5) unless an alert channel carries bot events or --i-accept-silent-failures is given

args.name: --i-accept-silent-failures
args.help: Acknowledge that no alert channel tells you if a bot halts, so --resume-recovering or --resume-halted may be used anyway

args.name: --confirm-venue
args.help: Type the mainnet venue to allow real-money bots to be started or resumed on it (--start-planned, --resume-recovering, --resume-halted). Without it --resume-recovering is refused (exit 2) when it would touch a mainnet venue, and --start-planned and --resume-halted skip the unconfirmed mainnet bots and say so (--start-planned also sends an alert) while the rest run

args.name: --skip-preflight
args.help: Do not run the pre-flight before serving. Logged as a WARNING; the key, the clock and the exchange are then not checked

apply.help: Make the bots match a plan file: create, edit and (with --prune) delete bots through the commands the Bots tab uses, and record each entry's desired_state for run --start-planned. Applying starts and stops nothing. A second apply of the same plan changes nothing. Beside a running host (main.py run) it asks the host entry by entry through the command directory instead of exiting 3: each entry is answered on its own, a refusal of one never stops the others, a host that stops answering leaves the rest listed as not sent, and a bot at rest is deleted only under --prune and only if it holds nothing. Exit 2 when an entry needs attention, 10 when no host is running, 5 when the running copy takes no commands, 11 when the host stops answering

stop.help: Ask the running host (main.py run) to stop one bot, as the Bots tab's Stop does: its orders are cancelled and it becomes STOPPED once none is left. A Spot bot keeps the coin it holds; a Futures bot is stopped only with --close-position, which closes its position at market (a position is never kept). If the venue's order session is closed (an Emergency Stop or a restart closes it) the host opens it first, as Start and Resume do; on a mainnet venue that needs --confirm-venue. Writes a command file only the host's account can write; changes nothing in this process. Exit 10 when no host is running, 5 when this account has no control over it

args.name: --close-position

Required for a Futures bot, whose position is never kept: without it the stop is refused and nothing changes. This trades at the market price, and on mainnet that is real money

The second of two steps: bot resume proposes, places nothing and prints the proposal with its fingerprint; you read it, then this lays that ladder and no other, naming it with --proposal. Refused in words when no proposal is held, when the held one is not the one you named (a later resume re-proposed), and when --proposal is missing. Exit 10 when no host is running, 5 when this account has no control over it

A HALTED or AWAITING_RECOVERY bot is refused: use bot resume then bot confirm-resume, run --resume-halted, or the Bots tab. The other bots are not touched. Exit 10 when no host is running, 5 when this account has no control over it

edit.help: Ask the running host (main.py run) to change the parameters of ONE DRAFT or STOPPED bot, as the Bots tab's Save does, while the other bots keep trading: bot edit <id> --set lower=81000 --set upper=90000. The same checks refuse an unknown parameter or an unreadable value in words and change nothing; any other state (RUNNING, PAUSED, HALTED, ...) is refused. Read the current values first with bot show <id> --params. The reply shows each change as old -> new. The bot lands on DRAFT; it places no order and needs no --confirm-venue, and is started by bot start, whose guard is unchanged. The plan file is yours and is NOT updated: change the same value in it too, or the next bot apply of the old plan edits the bot back. Exit 2 when the bot or the values are refused, 10 when no host is running, 5 when this account has no control over it

add.help: Ask the running host (main.py run) to create ONE bot from a plan file's entry, as the Bots tab's New bot does, while the other bots keep trading: bot add plan.json --name sol-grid. The bot lands DRAFT with the entry's parameters; it places no order, needs no --confirm-venue and is started by bot start, whose guard is unchanged. The plan's desired_state is ignored and nothing is recorded in state/bot_plan.json, so run --start-planned does not start it. A kind, venue or parameter the host cannot store, and a name already used on that venue, are refused in words and create nothing. Exit 2 when the plan entry is refused, 10 when no host is running, 5 when this account has no control over it

A bot in any other state, and a bot whose record still shows a held base, a live order or an order it owes, is refused in words and kept. Your plan file is not changed: delete the entry too, or the next bot apply creates the bot again. Exit 2 when the bot is refused, 10 when no host is running, 5 when this account has no control over it

A bot that has run, a Futures bot, a bot of the same name already on that venue, and a venue this build does not have are refused in words and nothing moves. Your plan file is not changed: change the entry's venue too, or the next bot apply creates a second bot. Exit 2 when the bot is refused, 10 when no host is running, 5 when this account has no control over it

The strategy, symbol, interval, sizing, leverage and parameters are the saved ones (the last successful arm; arm once from the desktop first) and are never typed here. An armed strategy places orders by itself, so on a mainnet venue --confirm-venue must repeat the venue. A venue that already has a strategy armed, a venue this run does not serve, no saved arming, and every refusal the tab shows (invalid parameters, a symbol leased by another strategy, a position open) are refused in words and nothing is armed. Exit 2 when refused, 10 when no host is running, 5 when this account has no control over it
